Review Title: ★ 1 Star
Review Text:
★ 1 Star — DoorDash Completely Ignored a Serious App Problem and Penalized Me for It

I’ve completed nearly 5,000 deliveries as a Dasher and have maintained a 95%+ acceptance rate and Platinum Dasher status. I know how the DoorDash app is supposed to work, which makes what happened—and DoorDash’s complete lack of response—even more frustrating.

On July 28th, I started dashing and was hit with 15 timed-out orders. The problem? The assignments NEVER showed up on my phone. They didn't appear on my screen for me to accept or decline. I never saw the restaurants, the payout, the distance, or any other information about these orders. They simply weren't there.

I couldn't accept them. I couldn't decline them. I never even had the opportunity to make a decision because DoorDash never delivered the assignments to my phone.

And to be clear, this isn't a case of me using some outdated phone that can't handle the DoorDash app. I have a current, top-of-the-line smartphone with 5G capabilities, with more than enough capability to run the DoorDash app. I've completed nearly 5,000 deliveries using the platform.

I immediately contacted DoorDash multiple times and explained exactly what was happening. I was told they would investigate the issue. I actually stopped dashing for 10 days to give DoorDash time to figure out what was wrong before I tried again.

During those 10 days, all I received were generic, form-letter responses essentially saying, “Here's your reference number, and we're looking into it.”

Apparently, they weren't looking into anything.

On August 7th, I tried dashing again, and the exact same thing happened. This time I caught the problem after another 5 assignments timed out, bringing my total to 20 timed-out orders.

Twenty orders.

NONE of these were declined orders. I did not decline them. The assignments never showed up on my phone.

Some of these were high-paying orders. Some were very short, easy deliveries that I would have gladly accepted. I never even got the chance to see them.

Yet DoorDash's system apparently considers all 20 of these as though I intentionally chose not to accept them.

The result? My acceptance rate went from over 95% down to 76%, putting my Platinum Dasher status at risk.

I've contacted DoorDash repeatedly. I've explained the problem. I've given them the dates. I've provided the reference numbers. I've stopped dashing for 10 days while they supposedly investigated. Then I tried again and experienced the exact same technical failure.

And what has DoorDash done?

Nothing.

They refuse to properly investigate the technical problem. They refuse to correct the 20 timed-out assignments. They refuse to restore my acceptance rate. And they refuse to restore the Platinum status that I earned through thousands of deliveries.

After nearly 5,000 dashes, I know the difference between an order I intentionally decline and an order that never appears on my phone in the first place.

If DoorDash's system fails to deliver an assignment to a Dasher's phone, the Dasher should not be penalized for it.

I did everything I was supposed to do. I reported the problem. I stopped working for 10 days to give them time to investigate. I tried again, and the exact same problem happened. I've repeatedly contacted support, and instead of actually fixing the problem, I've been given generic responses and reference numbers.

At this point, I have no confidence that anyone at DoorDash is actually investigating my situation.

DoorDash needs to take responsibility for its own technology instead of making Dashers pay the price for technical failures that are completely outside of their control.

Nearly 5,000 deliveries, a top-of-the-line 5G phone, a history of maintaining a 95%+ acceptance rate, and Platinum status—and apparently none of that matters when their system fails and their support team refuses to fix it.

If you're considering becoming a Dasher, understand that when something goes wrong with the DoorDash app, you may be completely on your own.

Extremely disappointed in DoorDash and their support. One star is generous.

Review Title: ⭐ 1 STAR
Review Text:
⭐ 1 STAR — DoorDash is NOT what you think it is

After using DoorDash repeatedly, I have to say that my experience has been extremely disappointing. Food frequently arrives late, cold, damaged, or poorly handled. And when there is a problem with the driver, getting meaningful help from DoorDash can be incredibly frustrating.

We have had drivers leave food without asking for the required delivery code. We have also had situations where the driver was late, the food was cold, and the pizza arrived crushed.

One incident went far beyond a bad delivery. We contacted DoorDash while the driver was still involved, and the driver became belligerent and cursed at me while DoorDash was on the phone. He was more concerned with leaving to make another delivery than addressing the fact that our order had arrived late and damaged. The situation became serious enough that a police report had to be filed.

What made it even more frustrating was DoorDash telling us that they couldn’t do anything because the driver was working through a third-party arrangement. That raises a very basic question: Who is actually responsible when something goes wrong?

DoorDash charges customers delivery fees, service fees, membership fees, and encourages tipping. Customers are essentially being asked to absorb more and more of the cost while the delivery experience can still be terrible.

And then there are the confusing options where you’re asked to pay extra if you want your order delivered immediately rather than having it bundled or delayed. If I’m already paying delivery and service fees, why should I have to pay even more just to receive the food I already ordered in a reasonable amount of time?

The biggest problem is accountability. When everything goes smoothly, DoorDash gets paid. But when something goes wrong, suddenly everyone has an excuse — the restaurant, the driver, the third-party company, or the customer.

DoorDash needs to take responsibility for the entire delivery experience, not just the transaction.

At the end of the day, DoorDash doesn’t feel like a reliable delivery service. It feels like a middleman collecting fees while customers are left dealing with the consequences when the system fails.

My advice: think twice before ordering. The fees aren’t worth it if your food arrives late, cold, crushed, or you can’t get meaningful help when something goes wrong.

Review Title: Unreliable drivers, zero accountability, and rising costs—I’m done with DoorDash.
Review Text:
I used to rely on DoorDash regularly, but the recent, rapid decline in service quality—paired with constantly escalating fees—has made it completely impossible to justify using this platform anymore. Between drivers mishandling orders and DoorDash refusing to take responsibility, the overall experience has become consistently frustrating.
Three recent experiences in a row demonstrate just how bad it’s gotten:
Instance 1 (Delivered someone else’s food): A driver completely mixed up orders and dropped off the wrong food while I was at work. Because of their carelessness, I was left without a lunch for the rest of my workday.
Instance 2 (40-minute grocery detour with my hot food): A driver picked up our restaurant order, but instead of bringing it to us, drove to a nearby Kroger and spent 40 minutes inside doing personal shopping or running another errand. The food arrived nearly an hour late and completely cold. When I reached out to DoorDash, they passed the buck and claimed they couldn't do anything because the order was placed through the restaurant’s app—leaving the local restaurant to take the financial hit and remake the food for a mistake the DoorDash driver made.
Instance 3 (Prioritizing distant deliveries over a 1-mile route): I ordered smoothies from a location just one mile from my office. The driver picked up my order, bypassed my office entirely, and drove significantly farther away to complete another delivery first. By the time my drinks were dropped off, they were completely melted into warm liquid.
It is ridiculous that customers are charged premium markups, service fees, and delivery charges only to receive melted drinks, cold food, or no lunch at all. DoorDash treats its customers and partner restaurants as collateral damage while taking no accountability for driver negligence.
I will no longer be giving DoorDash my business, and I strongly recommend ordering directly from local restaurants or using alternative services that actually value their customers.

Review Title: Title: Repeated documented issues and no confidence in DoorDash’s resolution process
Review Text:
7/21/26

I have been a regular DoorDash customer, and I don’t write negative reviews lightly. Unfortunately, after several documented issues over the past few weeks, I no longer have confidence in DoorDash’s customer support or escalation process.

My concerns began with multiple Starbucks deliveries from one location where my Frappuccinos repeatedly arrived significantly underfilled and often melted. I documented these deliveries with photographs because the issue became recurring. I reported these problems through DoorDash, but I did not feel they were resolved appropriately.

I eventually switched to a different Starbucks location, and the difference was immediate. My Frappuccinos arrived properly frozen, much closer to the expected fill level, and the espresso was noticeably stronger. That confirmed to me that the drink quality issue appeared to be specific to that Starbucks location—not every Starbucks.

However, what never improved was DoorDash’s handling of customer service.

On July 21, 2026, I placed a DoorDash Starbucks order that was marked as delivered, but I never received my food. I contacted DoorDash multiple times and was told my case had been escalated to a specialized team. I never received any follow-up, refund, or resolution. After waiting, I ultimately had to file a PayPal dispute, which is still pending.

Then, on August 1, 2026, I ordered dinner from another restaurant through DoorDash. I paid for two extra tzatziki sauces, but they were missing from the sealed bag. I was not asking for a refund of my meal—I requested reimbursement only for the missing paid add-on. DoorDash’s automated system immediately denied my request.

Because of my previous unresolved experience, I called customer support instead of relying on the app. The representative was courteous and professional, and I appreciate the way they treated me. However, I was once again told my case would be escalated to a specialized team—the same process that never resulted in a follow-up on my previous case.

My frustration isn’t about $1.50. It’s about confidence in the support process. Restaurants make mistakes. Drivers cannot verify the contents of sealed bags. I understand that.

What I don’t understand is why customers who document legitimate problems, report them promptly, and ask only for reimbursement of missing paid items are left feeling that their concerns disappear into an escalation process with no meaningful follow-up.

I sincerely hope DoorDash improves both its automated refund system and its escalation process because customers deserve to know that documented issues will actually be reviewed and resolved.
